title: Playing along with a written part

cues.show: You with the guitar, the play-along stopped on screen.
cues.say: This is the play-along. It gives you a part to play in time, one step on each beat, with a metronome and a piano under you.

cues.show: Point along the tab: a strum, a single note, notes stacked together.
cues.say: The tab has six lines, one for each string, with the thickest string at the bottom. The numbers are frets.

cues.show: Point along the tab: a strum, a single note, notes stacked together.
cues.say: Numbers stacked on top of each other are played together. The line above the tab names the chord you are on.

cues.show: Press the Play button and listen to one loop without playing.
cues.say: Press the Play button below to start it. It starts straight away and goes round until you stop it.

cues.show: Press the Play button and listen to one loop without playing.
cues.say: Listen to one round first, and follow the lit step with your eyes.

cues.show: Play along for a few loops, counting aloud.
cues.say: Now play along. If you miss a step, leave it and come back in on the next beat 1.

cues.show: Use − under Tempo to slow down, then play again.
cues.say: Under Tempo, the minus button makes it slower. Slow gives you time to place each note.

cues.show: Use − under Tempo to slow down, then play again.
cues.say: Practice until you play the whole loop without stopping.

cues.show: Press notes, then neck, then tab. Change one thing in the part.
cues.say: Try things with it. Above the tab, press notes to see the note names, or neck to see the part on the guitar neck.

cues.show: Press notes, then neck, then tab. Change one thing in the part.
cues.say: Play the part louder on beat 1. Leave one step out and let it be silent.

cues.show: Press notes, then neck, then tab. Change one thing in the part.
cues.say: Then change the part a little: swap a single note for a strum and hear what it does.
